text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today to $140.52, giving back some of Friday's gains after hitting a two-week high of $142.28 the day before. The move comes as oil prices softened slightly—U.S. crude dropped to $89.62 per barrel from levels that had supported the stock's recent climb—and follows a week of volatility in which geopolitical risk (Iran escalating threats in the Middle East on November 17th) initially pushed prices higher but then failed to sustain the rally.

The stock's broader 4.3% decline over two weeks reflects uncertainty about which way oil demand and supply will tip. While heating oil prices are up sharply year-over-year, suggesting strong seasonal demand, cautious retail inventory planning for the holidays signals weakening downstream economic activity. That tension—between tight supply costs and softer consumer demand—is playing out in the stock's zigzag pattern.
